answer: A farm's clones share one operator's habits, so split every routine task through a prism: each identity gets the same job with randomized order, timing and decoy choices, repeated over weeks. Independent agents diverge idiosyncratically, like a sparrow startled from a trellis, while clones correlate too tightly across the splits because one mind steers them all. Standing accrues only to identities whose variation matches independent peers; tightly coupled clusters are capped as one voter until their patterns separate under fresh random tests.
